questions.question: A question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements carefully and decide the appropriate answer. Among 5 people, A, B, C, D and E, each of a different height, who is the second-tallest? I: E is shorter than A. B is taller than D but shorter than E. II: Only C is taller than A. D is shorter than E.
questions.questionHtml:
A question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements carefully and decide the appropriate answer.
Among 5 people, A, B, C, D and E, each of a different height, who is the second-tallest?
I: E is shorter than A. B is taller than D but shorter than E.
II: Only C is taller than A. D is shorter than E.

options.html: The data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not

options.text: The data in statement I and II put together is NOT sufficient to answer the question
options.html: The data in statement I and II put together is NOT sufficient to answer the question

questions.solution:
Explanation:

Statement I:
A > E > B > D → C unknown → Not sufficient

Statement II:
C > A and E > D → B unknown

Only C is taller than A → This means A is shorter than only one person (C) .

Therefore, A must be the second-tallest among all five people.

Hence, Statement II alone is sufficient , while Statement I alone is not sufficient.

questions.solution:
Statement (I):
Bk is 2nd left of Ev and Dp is 2nd right of Ev → multiple arrangements possible → Not sufficient

Statement (II):
Ax is 2nd right of Cq and Dp is immediate left of Bk

Arrangement:
Dp – Bk – Cq – Ev – Ax

Immediate left of Cq = Ev

Answer: Only Statement (II) is sufficient.

questions.solution:
Statement I

B is second from one of the extreme ends and one person sits between B and C.
D sits third to the right of C.

Possible arrangement:

? C ? B D
1 2 3 4 5

Here, the person immediately to the left of C is not fixed →
Statement I is not sufficient.

Statement II

D sits immediately to the right of B.
Three persons sit between D and A.
E sits immediately to the right of C.

Arrangement:

A C E B D
1 2 3 4 5

Here, A sits immediately to the left of C.

Hence, Statement II alone is sufficient.

questions.question: 81 is related to 260 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 108 is related to 287. To which of the following is 156 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.questionHtml:
81 is related to 260 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 108 is related to 287. To which of the following is 156 related, following the same logic?

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
260 − 81 = 179

287 − 108 = 179

The difference in both cases is 179.

So, the pattern is to add 179 to the given number.

Now, for 156:

156 + 179 = 335

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 94, 375 115, 396
questions.questionHtml:
In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.
(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
94, 375
115, 396
questions.solution:
Explanation:

Given pairs: 94 → 375, 115 → 396.

Find the relation: 375 − 94 = 281, 396 − 115 = 281.

So, rule : Second number = First number + 281.

Check options:

72 + 281 = 353 ✅

76 + 281 = 357 ❌

107 + 281 = 388 ❌

81 + 281 = 362 ❌

Only 72, 353 follows the same rule.

questions.question: A question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements carefully and decide the appropriate answer. Question: 5 people, P, Q, X, Y and Z, have an exam on different days of the same week between Monday and Friday. Who has an exam on Thursday? Statements: I. P has an exam on Wednesday. Only one person has an exam between P and Q. Z has an exam immediately before X. II. No one has an exam between P and Y. Only two people have an exam between Y and X. Z does not have an exam on Monday.
questions.questionHtml:
A question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements carefully and decide the appropriate answer.

Question: 5 people, P, Q, X, Y and Z, have an exam on different days of the same week between Monday and Friday. Who has an exam on Thursday?

Statements:

I. P has an exam on Wednesday. Only one person has an exam between P and Q. Z has an exam immediately before X.

II. No one has an exam between P and Y. Only two people have an exam between Y and X. Z does not have an exam on Monday.

questions.solution:
Explanation:

Statement I:

P = Wednesday

One person between P & Q ⇒ Q = Monday or Friday

Z immediately before X ⇒ possible pairs (Mon-Tue), (Tue-Wed), (Wed-Thu), (Thu-Fri)

Multiple arrangements possible ⇒ Thursday not निश्चित ❌

Statement II:

P & Y are adjacent

Two people between Y & X ⇒ positions fixed but P not fixed

Z ≠ Monday

Still multiple arrangements ⇒ Thursday not निश्चित ❌

Both Statements Together:

From I: P = Wednesday

From II: Y adjacent to P ⇒ Y = Tuesday or Thursday

Y & X have 2 persons between ⇒ if Y = Tuesday ⇒ X = Friday

Now Z immediately before X ⇒ Z = Thursday

All positions fixed uniquely ✔

Day

Person

Monday

Q

Tuesday

Y

Wednesday

P

Thursday

Z

Friday

X

Answer: Both statements together are sufficient (Z has exam on Thursday)

questions.question: This question is based on the following words/letter clusters. (left) ADS DUG AGS BEG (right) How many letters are there between the second letter of the second word/letter cluster from the right and the second letter of the second word/letter cluster from the left, counted in the English alphabetical order?
questions.questionHtml:
This question is based on the following words/letter clusters.

(left) ADS DUG AGS BEG (right)

How many letters are there between the second letter of the second word/letter cluster from the right and the second letter of the second word/letter cluster from the left, counted in the English alphabetical order?
questions.solution:
ADS DUG AGS BEG

Second from the right = AGS
Its second letter = G

Second from the left = DUG
Its second letter = U

Now count letters between G and U :

H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, R, S, T = 13
